title: Gimel Track — Reading with Meaning
description: A 32-lesson reading course that builds from accurate decoding into familiar vocabulary, phrases, and connected meaning.

lessons.title: Reading with Meaning
lessons.focus: See the letters, read the word from right to left, then explain its meaning.
lessons.cue: Point to each letter in אוֹר. Read or first; look for light only after you have decoded it.
lessons.question: What does אוֹר mean?

lessons.title: Notice the Sun Word
lessons.focus: Read from the first letter on the right. Let the two syllables stay clear: she-mesh.
lessons.cue: Point to each letter as you read; then cover the picture and tell what the word means.
lessons.question: Which meaning belongs to שֶׁמֶשׁ?

lessons.title: Read a Hand Word
lessons.focus: Blend the vowel and finish with ד, Dalet. Do not add an extra vowel after the last letter.
lessons.cue: Touch the final letter only after you have read the vowel.
lessons.question: Which meaning belongs to יָד?

lessons.title: Read a Sea Word
lessons.focus: Read right to left and close the word with final Mem, ם.
lessons.cue: Stretch the vowel briefly, then close with m.
lessons.question: Which meaning belongs to יָם?

lessons.title: Read Water in Two Beats
lessons.focus: Hear the word in two beats: ma-yim. The final ם keeps its m sound.
lessons.cue: Say both beats, then blend them into one word.
lessons.question: What does מַיִם mean?

lessons.title: Read a House Word
lessons.focus: Read the Bet first, then follow the vowel pattern toward Tav. The word names a place to live.
lessons.cue: Read before looking at the picture. Point to a house only after you say the word.
lessons.question: Which meaning belongs to בַּיִת?

lessons.title: Read a Bread Word
lessons.focus: Read the two parts slowly, then close with ם. Follow your teacher’s model for ח.
lessons.cue: Do not guess from the picture; use the letters and vowels first.
lessons.question: Which meaning belongs to לֶחֶם?

lessons.title: Read a Strawberry Word
lessons.focus: The two ת letters frame the oo sound. Keep the word short and clear.
lessons.cue: Point to the middle vowel, then say the first and last sounds.
lessons.question: Which word means strawberry?

lessons.title: Compare Sea and Hand
lessons.focus: The first letter and vowel are alike. The final consonant changes the word’s meaning.
lessons.cue: Read both words, then point to the final letter that makes them different.
lessons.question: Which final letter closes the word for hand?

lessons.title: Ask Who?
lessons.focus: This short word asks about a person. Read it as one smooth syllable.
lessons.cue: Ask “מִי?” and invite a partner to answer with a person’s name.
lessons.question: What does מִי ask?

lessons.title: Use a Greeting
lessons.focus: Read the parts sha-lom. The same greeting can open or close a conversation.
lessons.cue: Say shalom to a partner, then use it again when you part.
lessons.question: Which word can mean hello or goodbye?

lessons.title: Read Mother
lessons.focus: Use the class pronunciation model. Read the whole word before connecting it to a person.
lessons.cue: Say the word gently, then point to the matching family picture.
lessons.question: Which word means mother?

lessons.title: Read Father
lessons.focus: Notice the repeated sound pattern. Read both syllables without rushing.
lessons.cue: Read the word, then use it in a greeting: שָׁלוֹם אַבָּא.
lessons.question: Which word means father?

lessons.title: Read Son
lessons.focus: Start at Bet and finish with final Nun, ן. The last form changes shape, not sound.
lessons.cue: Find ן at the end and keep its n sound.
lessons.question: Which word means son?

lessons.title: Read a Book Word
lessons.focus: Read the vowel under Samech, then the two syllables. Follow your teacher’s pronunciation for Peh.
lessons.cue: Read the word first. Then choose a book and say סֵפֶר.
lessons.question: Which word means book?

lessons.title: Read Child
lessons.focus: Read both short syllables and finish with Dalet. A word can name a person.
lessons.cue: Say the word, then show the picture that matches it.
lessons.question: Which word means boy or child?

lessons.title: Read Girl
lessons.focus: Compare this word with יֶלֶד. Notice how a different ending can change the word.
lessons.cue: Read both words aloud with a teacher, then sort the matching pictures.
lessons.question: Which word means girl?

lessons.title: Read Heart
lessons.focus: The final ב without a dot is read as v in this word. Keep the final sound soft.
lessons.cue: Read the word, then connect “heart” to a feeling or kind action.
lessons.question: Which meaning belongs to לֵב?

lessons.title: Read Friend
lessons.focus: Follow the teacher’s model for ח. Read both syllables before naming the relationship.
lessons.cue: Read the word, then use it to greet a friend.
lessons.question: Which word means friend?

lessons.title: Read Good
lessons.focus: The over vowel gives oh here. Finish with Bet, which is soft after the vowel.
lessons.cue: Read טוֹב, then use it with a picture or object you like.
lessons.question: What does טוֹב mean?

lessons.title: Read Day
lessons.focus: Read the whole word as one beat. Final Mem closes the word.
lessons.cue: Say יוֹם and point to a picture of daytime.
lessons.question: Which word means day?

lessons.title: Read Song
lessons.focus: Find the dot on the right side of ש for Shin. Read the vowel and finish with Resh.
lessons.cue: Read the word, then hum a short tune you know.
lessons.question: Which word means song?

lessons.title: Read Voice
lessons.focus: The Qof begins the word. Read the oh pattern and close with Lamed.
lessons.cue: Say קוֹל softly and loudly; notice that the meaning stays the same.
lessons.question: Which word means voice or sound?

lessons.title: Read Flower
lessons.focus: Read the first syllable, then follow the vowel under Resh. Use your teacher’s model for ח.
lessons.cue: Trace the word from right to left and match it to a flower.
lessons.question: Which word means flower?

lessons.title: Read Bird
lessons.focus: The first letter is Tsadi. Read all three parts slowly, then blend them.
lessons.cue: Point to each sound. Use the picture only after you have decoded the word.
lessons.question: Which word means bird?

lessons.title: Read Tree
lessons.focus: The final form ץ is Tsadi at the end of a word. Its shape changes, but its sound remains.
lessons.cue: Find the final letter and say its sound without adding a vowel.
lessons.question: Which word means tree?

lessons.title: Read King
lessons.focus: Final Kaf ך appears at the end. The small sheva here closes the word; follow the teacher’s model.
lessons.cue: Read the word, then point to final ך. Do not add another syllable.
lessons.question: Which word means king?

lessons.title: Read Silver
lessons.focus: Kaf begins the word and final Peh ף closes it. A final letter keeps its familiar sound.
lessons.cue: Find the two letters with changed or dotted forms, then read the word.
lessons.question: Which word means silver or money?

lessons.title: Read Land
lessons.focus: The word ends with final Tsadi ץ. Read to the end without adding an extra vowel.
lessons.cue: Point to the final form and compare it with צ at the start of צִפּוֹר.
lessons.question: Which word means land or earth?

lessons.title: Say “This Is a Book”
lessons.focus: Read each word, then join them. זֶה points to something nearby; סֵפֶר names it.
lessons.cue: Place a book nearby, point to it, and say זֶה סֵפֶר.
lessons.question: What does זֶה סֵפֶר mean?

lessons.title: Ask “What Is This?”
lessons.focus: Read the question words together. Let your voice show that you are asking.
lessons.cue: Point to a familiar object and ask מַה זֶה? Let your partner answer.
lessons.question: Which phrase asks “What is this?”

lessons.title: Read “I Have a Book”
lessons.focus: Read the phrase in three parts. Keep the spaces between words, then say the whole idea.
lessons.cue: Hold a book and say the phrase. Then trade roles with a partner.
lessons.question: What does יֵשׁ לִי סֵפֶר mean?
